newsitem.title: CANADA: Saskatchewan forecasts early seeding out west.
newsitem.headline: Saskatchewan forecasts early seeding out west.

text.p: Spring seeding of Saskatchewan crops was forecast to begin by month's end in the western region of the province, ahead of normal, Saskatchewan Agriculture said.
"Field work is beginning in western regions of the province where seeding is anticipated to start by the end of April - ahead of normal," a Saskatchewan Ag statement said.
Eastern regions need one to two weeks of warm, dry weather before field work and seeding starts at about the normal seeding time for that part of the province, the statement said.
Sunny and above normal temperatures advanced anticipated seeding schedules in the west and snow melt in the northeast.
Seeding usually begins by May 7 across the Prairies, the Canadian Wheat Board has said.

"Compared to last year, farmers indicated that fertilizer uas is expected to be up nearly four percent in central and two percent in northern regions, while southern regions are expected to increase by six percent," Saskatchewan Ag said.
There were adequate supplies of fertilizer, herbicides and seeds across Saskatchewan, it said.
Harvest of crops that overwintered should begin in central Saskatchewan this week and in northern regions the first week of May, it said.
